steps.title: In the ground
steps.text: Tantalum's main ore is columbite-tantalite, known in Central Africa as coltan, found in pegmatites and in the gravels weathered from them. It is also a by-product of lithium mining in Australia and of tin smelting.
steps.india: No deposit is worked commercially. The Atomic Minerals Directorate holds 149 t of columbite-tantalite from prospecting.

steps.title: Mine
steps.text: In DR Congo, Rwanda and Nigeria most tantalum is dug by hand from pits and stream beds by small-scale miners. Tracing where it came from, and keeping it out of armed groups' hands, shapes the whole trade. Brazil and Australia mine it mechanically.

steps.title: Concentrate
steps.text: The mineral is heavy, so it is washed and tabled by gravity, then cleaned with magnets.

steps.title: Dissolve and separate
steps.text: The concentrate is dissolved in hydrofluoric and sulphuric acid. Tantalum and niobium, chemical twins that always occur together, are pulled apart by solvent extraction. Tantalum is crystallised as a potassium fluoride salt. China is the largest processor, with about 43%.

steps.title: Reduce
steps.text: The salt is reacted with molten sodium, which leaves a fine tantalum powder. For wire and sheet the powder is melted in an electron beam under vacuum.

steps.title: Make
steps.text: Powder is pressed around a tantalum wire and sintered into a porous pellet with a huge surface area: the anode of a capacitor. Tantalum is also made into sputtering targets, sheet and tube.
steps.india: The Nuclear Fuel Complex makes tantalum pentoxide and tantalum metal in small quantities.

steps.title: Use
steps.text: Tantalum capacitors pack more charge into less space than any other kind and are very reliable, so they are in phones, cars, pacemakers and satellites. In chips, a tantalum layer stops copper wiring from leaking into the silicon. The metal resists acid and is used in chemical plant and implants.
steps.india: Electronics and semiconductor demand, all imported.

steps.title: Recycle
steps.text: Scrap from capacitor and target making is recovered, as is superalloy scrap. Tantalum in discarded electronics is mostly lost.
